newsitem.title: USA: Empire of Carolina sees 1996 EPS shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Empire of Carolina sees 1996 EPS shortfall.

text.p: Empire of Carolina said it expects its 1996 fiscal year earnings to be lower than analysts' expectations because of a drop in re-orders during the fourth quarter.

The re-order shortfall will result in "significantly" lower-than-expected sales for the fourth quarter, the company said. It did not provide details and officials were not immediately available to comment.
According to estimates from First Call the company was expected to report a loss of $3.38 per share for 1996, including a loss of $0.36 per share in the fourth quarter.
But it said it might not have enough cash on hand to fund its operations if it fails to reach a credit arrangement with the lenders.
The company said it was talking with investment bankers to "evaluate strategic alternatives for enhancing shareholder value".
It was also trying to get from the bankers the additional financing required by the December 6, 1996 amendment to its senior loan agreement, it added.
The company also said its president and chief operating officer, Marvin Smollar, would no longer be involved in the management of the company even though he would remain on the board of directors.
A replacement for Smollar had yet been named, it said.
Empire of Caroline makes plastic toys for children.
